questions.q: What problem does Spark actually solve?
options: Processing data too large to fit in one machine's memory, by spreading it across a cluster of many machines
Making Python code run without any syntax errors
Replacing the need for a code editor
Converting CSV files into JSON automatically
questions.explain: Spark coordinates many machines working on slices of data in parallel.

questions.q: Why does Pandas eventually stop working on very large datasets?
options: Pandas runs entirely on one machine's memory, and runs out of memory once the data is too large
Pandas has a hard-coded row limit of exactly 1,000 rows
Pandas cannot read CSV files larger than 1MB
Pandas automatically switches to Spark when data gets too large
questions.explain: A single month of taxi data fits fine; the full historical dataset spanning back to 2009 would not.

questions.q: What was Spark's key improvement over its predecessor, Hadoop MapReduce?
options: Doing intermediate processing steps in memory instead of writing to disk between every step, making multi-step processing dramatically faster
Spark removed the need for a cluster entirely
Spark only works with JSON, while MapReduce only worked with CSV
There was no real improvement — they are functionally identical
questions.explain: MapReduce's disk-based intermediate results were reliable but slow; Spark's in-memory approach solved that.

questions.q: What does a 'cluster' mean in the context of Spark?
options: Multiple machines working together on one computation, coordinated to behave like a single large computation
A single powerful machine with many CPU cores but no networking
A type of file format
A synonym for a Pandas DataFrame
questions.explain: Spark's coordination is what makes many separate machines appear, from your code, like one big computation.

questions.q: What does this chapter (Apache Spark Fundamentals) build toward?
options: The conceptual foundation Chapter 4's hands-on PySpark work assumes you already have
A complete replacement for everything taught in Chapter 2
Only theoretical knowledge with no practical application anywhere in this course
Skills unrelated to any later chapter in this course
questions.explain: Architecture, partitions, lazy evaluation, and SparkSession all directly prepare for Chapter 4's real PySpark code.
